'''''Smilax aspera''''', with [[common name]]s '''common smilax''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''rough bindweed''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=SMAS|taxon=Smilax aspera|accessdate=2 February 2016}}</ref> '''sarsaparille''',<ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=smilax+aspera Altervista Flora Italiana, salsapariglia, sarsaparille, rough bindweed, ''Smilax aspera''] includes photos and European distribution map</ref> and '''Mediterranean smilax''', is a species of [[Flowering plant|flowering]] [[vine]] in the [[Smilacaceae|greenbriar family]].

==Description==
''Smilax aspera'' is a  [[perennial]], evergreen climber with a flexible and delicate stem, with sharp thorns. The climbing stem is {{convert|1|-|4|m}} long.<ref name=Pignatti>Pignatti S. - Flora d'Italia – Edagricole – 1982. Vol. III, pag. 401</ref>  The leaves are {{convert|8|-|10|cm}} long,<ref name=Pignatti/> petiolated, alternate, tough, leathery, and heart-shaped, with toothed and spiny margins. It is a [[Monocotyledon|monocot]] with reticulate venation.  The midrib of the underside of the leaf is also provided with spines.  The flowers, very fragrant, are small, yellowish or greenish, gathered in axillary [[raceme]]s. The flowering period in Mediterranean regions extends from September to November. The fruits are globose berries, gathered in clusters, which ripen in autumn. They are initially red, later turning black. They have a diameter of {{convert|8|-|10|mm}}<ref name=Pignatti/> and contain one to three tiny and round seeds. They are insipid and unpalatable to humans, but they are a source of nourishment for many species of birds.

==Distribution==
This species is widespread in  Central [[Africa]] (Democratic Republic of [[Democratic Republic of the Congo|Congo]], [[Kenya]], [[Ethiopia]]), Mediterranean [[Europe]] ([[Cyprus]], [[Albania]], [[Croatia]], [[Greece]], [[Italy]], [[Malta]], Montenegro, [[France]], [[Portugal]], [[Spain]]), temperate [[Asia]] ( [[Israel]], [[Jordan]], [[Lebanon]], [[Syria]], [[Turkey]]) and tropical [[Asia]]  ([[India]], [[Bhutan]], [[Nepal]]). It is also naturalized in other regions.<ref name=GRIN>{{GRIN | accessdate=6 August 2014}}</ref>

==Habitat==
It grows in woods and scrub at an altitude of {{convert|0|-|1200|m}} above sea level.<ref name=Pignatti/>
